description.narrative: 4.1 – Initial work on the scoresheet Local partner organizations will initiate the FTM work by analyzing and filling the scoresheetdocument provided by ON and TJN-A. The scoresheet will provide an initial perspective of the national context in relationto tax <(>&<)> gender aspects. This will provide focus and indicate possible areas/topics that will require further attention and possible recommendations for future advocacy work. As the local partner organization works on the scoresheet, the researchers mayreach out to ONand TJN-A at any moment in case of any issues or questions related to a scoring question. Once completed, the scoresheet will be sent to ON and TJN-A. ON and TJN-A will review and provide feedback on the scoresheet until a final version is agreed upon. 4.2 – Prioritization workshop Following the completion of the scoresheet, the local partner organization will hold a prioritization workshop with relevant allies, civil society organizations and stakeholders in the country. In the workshop, the local partner organization will discuss the GET FTM project, present the early findings of the scoresheet research and receive input on the most significant topics and areas that the national report should focus on. The purpose of this workshop isto identify the topics that should be prioritized in the upcoming national reports, as well as recognize possible topics for national advocacy work. 4.3 – Draft of national report The researcher of each local partner organization will then begin to write the national report utilizing the GET FTM methodology provided. To ensure the production of a high quality research, it is important that the researcher takes into account the background information (including the Gender and Tax FTM 2019 report) and the scoresheet previously analyzed. As the FTM is an advocacy tool, it is important to make the output not only descriptive, but political, normative and prescriptive. Local partner organizations will be able to contact ON and TJN-A for technical support at all stages of the research process, and feedback will be provided promptly.ON and TJN-A will reinforce at all opportunities their availability to provide technical support at any moment a local partner organization encounters issues or have questions regarding the project. Monthly update calls will be scheduled with each of the local partner organizations to keep track of the progress in the research and clarify any questions along the process. EF will be invited tojoin such meetings. The local partners will be required to submit an updated version of their draft research in advance of the monthly update calls, so ON and TJN-A are able to review the work and be aware of the current status of the research and potential issues. In addition to individual periodical meetings with each local partner organization, ON and TJN-A will organize bi-monthly collective calls with all local partner organizations present (once every two months). The main purpose of these meetings is to foster peerto peer collaboration and the exchange of common obstacles and solutions towards the work. EF will be invited to join such meetings. Both for the monthly update calls and for the bi-monthly collective calls, ON and TJN-A will consider the impact of language barriers (inrelation to the representative of each local partner organization) and potential solutions to it (possibly including the presence of translators). Following the finalization of the first draft of the national report, the local partner organization will submit the document to ON and TJN-A. Input and recommendations will be provided through multiple rounds of feedback – through e-mails and video calls – until a satisfactory final version is agreed upon. The final version of the chapter will also include selected recommendations. After ON, TJN-A and the local partner organization have reached a satisfactory final version of the document, EF will have the opportunity to review the document. In case of any input and recommendation from EF, such feedback will be implemented by ON,TJN-A and the local partner organization until all parties are satisfied with the final version. 4.4 – National validation session Once the national report is finalized by a local partner organization, a validation session will be held at the country. Validation sessions should ideally include multiple stakeholders, including representatives from national tax administrations and finance ministries, academics, private sector representatives and civil society organizations. Ideally– and depending on each national context – EF could play a role in identifying and inviting government and private sector representatives to the validation sessions. The session will include a presentation of the report and its main findings to the multiple stakeholders, followed by discussions on the document and input into the main text. In that sense, the validation session provides an opportunity for local partner organizations to establish a concrete work relationship with external stakeholders andto be recognized as a reliable collaborator on public policy. Any recommendations, input or corrections provided during the validation sessions by the stakeholders will be considered for incorporation at the final version of the draft, through consensus decisions taken by the local partner organization, ON, TJN-A and EF.

participating-org.narrative:
Social Watch is an international network of citizens’ organizations in the struggle to eradicate poverty and the causes of poverty,to end all forms of discrimination and racism, to ensure an equitable distribution of wealth and the realization of human rights. We are committed to peace, social, economic, environment and gender justice, and we emphasize the right of all people not to be poor.
Social Watch holds governments, the UN system and international organizations accountable for the fulfillment of national, regional and international commitments to eradicate poverty.
Social Watch will achieve its objectives through a comprehensive strategy of advocacy, awareness-building, monitoring, organizational development and networking. Social Watch promotes people-centred sustainable development.
